newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Qualcomm plans Ukraine telcoms production.
newsitem.headline: Qualcomm plans Ukraine telcoms production.

text.p: U.S. communications firm Qualcomm Inc plans to produce telecommunications equipment in Ukraine from next year, its president said late on Thursday.
"We're starting out with investments in the range of $10-$20 million," chief executive Irwin Jacobs said. "We're hoping to start deploying this service in 1997."

Qualcomm, the patent holder for the CDMA digital cellular system, has formed a joint venture with Telesystemy Ukrainy to manufacture telephones at a microelectronics factory in the eastern city of Dnipropetrovsk.
Jacobs said Qualcomm aimed to make 250,000 telephones a year when production began in mid-1997.
He said this would be the first attempt to bring local wireless communications to Ukraine, where only eight million out of 52 million people have telephones.
Telesystemy Ukrainy owns 51 percent of the joint venture and Qualcomm 49 percent. Under Ukrainian law a Ukrainian company must be the majority partner in a telecoms joint venture.
Ukraine's state monopoly company Ukrtelekom has signed framework agreements with several foreign firms to manufacture and install ports and switches until 2005, estimated to cost $20 billion.
Jacobs, who met President Leonid Kuchma this week, said that Qualcomm planned to eventually increase investment to $2 billion providing the system was accepted in Ukraine.

"We hope to have capacity sufficient to supply the needs of Ukraine and export to other countries," he said, adding that the company eventually hoped to manufacture station parts for mobile communications.

Telesystemy Ukrainy executive Viktor Zhylinsky said the company planned to begin production on June 1 1997, and that the system would initially be deployed in the Kiev, Dnipropetrovsk, Odessa, Lviv and Ternopil areas.

Jacobs said he was confident the company would receive frequencies. Some mobile companies have recently threatened to pull investments when the government failed to deliver frequencies, raised tariffs, and changed licensing requirements.
"Things are moving as far as frequencies," he said. "We have locations for radio antennas and connections to phone systems."
Qualcomm also planned to provide ground equipment in Ukraine for its Globalstar satellite in 1998-1999, Irwin added.
